response.justification: The candidate is an accomplished full-stack/web engineer with 15+ years of experience, but the resume shows essentially no overlap with the core requirements of a Principal Performance Architect for AI accelerators. There is no evidence of SoC or IP modeling, hardware-software co-design, GPU/SIMD/MIMD architecture, deep neural network training or inference optimization, or silicon performance analysis. The only adjacent signals are brief C/C++ work at National Instruments, some robotics/embedded exposure, and low-latency service optimization at Sociomantic — none of which approaches principal-level hardware architecture. Education is a BS in Computer Science with sufficient years of experience to meet the formal threshold, but the technical domain mismatch is decisive.
strengths: 15+ years of broad software engineering experience, including staff-level roles
Some low-level exposure: C/C++ at National Instruments, embedded/robotics, high-throughput low-latency services
Strong engineering rigor — TDD, CI/CD, open-source tooling, public talks and workshops
concerns: No SoC/IP modeling, hardware architecture, or hardware-software co-design experience
No deep learning, GPU, SIMD/MIMD, or AI accelerator workload optimization background
Career trajectory is web/full-stack, not silicon performance architecture at principal level

key_factors.factor: Missing SoC/IP modeling and hardware architecture experience
No AI accelerator / deep-learning workload optimization background
Extensive senior software engineering track record and systems performance work
